sections.body: Some things about you are PRIVATE. That means just for you and your family. 🔒
Private things are: your full name, home address, phone number, school, passwords and photos of you.
Online, people may not be who they say they are. A 'kid' online could really be a grown-up.
If anyone online asks for private things, stop. Tell a grown-up you trust.
Agree on simple family rules: never share private details online, and always tell a parent if someone asks. Praise your child for telling you, even if they already shared something.

quiz.q: A game asks for your home address. What do you do?
hints: Who can help you decide what is safe?
If a stranger at the park asked where you live, you would find your grown-up. Online is the same.
quiz.explain: Your address is private. Always ask a grown-up first.

hints: Private things could help someone find you or get into your accounts.
Which one keeps your games and apps locked?
A house key is private because it opens your door. What is the online 'key'?
quiz.explain: A password is like a key. Never share it, except with your parents.

quiz.q: Someone online says they are 8 years old. Can you be sure?
hints: Can you see the person online?
If someone wrote 'I am a dinosaur' in a message, would that make it true?
quiz.explain: Online, anyone can pretend. That's why we keep private things private.
